translations.text: An instruction delivered by our holy father, honored in every way, Apa Pachomius, the archimandrite,
the holy one, concerning a brother who became angry with someone in the time of Apa Ebonh. After bringing him to Tabennese, he spoke these words to him.
Other elderly fathers were also there, rejoicing greatly in the peace of God.
May his holy blessings and the blessings of all the saints come down upon you, and may we all be saved. Amen.
My son, listen and become wise, and accept true instruction.
For there are two ways.
Either make yourself worthy and obey God like Abraham, who left his land and committed himself to living as a foreigner, dwelling in tents with Isaac in the promised land as a stranger.
He obeyed and humbled himself, and he was brought into an inheritance, until he was tested concerning Isaac.
He remained strong in the trial and offered Isaac up as a sacrifice to God.
Because of this, God called him “my friend.”
Take for yourself also Jacob’s humility, simplicity, and endurance, until he became a light, seeing the Father of all, and was called Israel.
Take for yourself also Joseph’s wisdom and simplicity, and struggle with self-control and servitude until you become a king.
My son, strive to imitate the lives of the saints, and live according to their virtues.
Wake yourself up.
Do not be negligent.
Rouse your fellow citizen, for whom you have stood surety.
Rise up; do not remain with the dead, so that Christ may shine upon you and grace may shine within you.
For it is patience that reveals all the gifts to you. The saints were patient and obtained the promises.
The glory of the saints is patience.
Be patient, so that you may be counted among the saints, believing that you will receive an imperishable crown.
A thought—bear with it patiently until God gives you relief.
A fast—endure it with perseverance.
Prayer without ceasing in your private room, between you and God alone.
One heart with your brother.
Virginity in every part of your body.
Virginity in your thoughts.
Purity of body and purity of heart.
A bowed neck and a humble heart.
Gentleness in a time of anger.
If a thought weighs heavily on you, do not lose heart, but endure joyfully, saying, “They surrounded me on every side,
but I drove them back in the name of the Lord.”
Immediately God’s help will come to you, and you will drive them away from you. Joy will surround you, and God’s glory will walk with you.
For joy walks with the humble, and you will be satisfied as your soul desires.
For God’s paths are humility of heart and gentleness.
For he said, “On whom will I look except the humble and gentle?”
If you walk in the Lord’s paths, the Lord will watch over you and strengthen you.
He will fill you with knowledge and wisdom, and your remembrance of him will remain before him at all times. He will rescue you from the devil and grant you his peace at your end.
My son, I command you to keep watch and remain sober, knowing those who lie in wait for you.
The spirit of cowardice and the spirit of unbelief walk together.
The spirit of falsehood and the spirit of deceitfulness walk together.
The spirit of love of money, the spirit of trading, the spirit of swearing falsely, the spirit of wickedness, and evildoing walk together.
The spirit of vanity and the spirit of arrogance walk together.
The spirit of sexual immorality and impurity walk together.
The spirit of hostility and the spirit of sorrow walk together.
But woe to the wretched soul whom they seize and rule over! They make such a soul stray from God,
because it has come under their power, distracted this way and that until it reaches the pits of the underworld.
My son, listen to me; do not be careless.
Do not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids, so that you may escape like a gazelle from snares.
For all these spirits, my son, have troubled me many times since my childhood.
While I was in the wilderness, they would oppress me until my heart grew faint, so that I thought, “I do not have the strength to stand against the dragon’s threat.”
For he harasses me on every side.
Whenever I come among others, he gathers them against me, and they fight me.
Whenever I withdraw, he oppresses me with his persistence.
My heart has grown numb within me. Many times I turn in every direction and find no rest.
But whenever I run to God with weeping and humility, with fasting and nights of keeping watch,
the enemy grows weak before me, along with all his other spirits, and the joy of God comes to me.
And immediately I recognize God's help, because through his patience he teaches human beings about his power and his goodness.
My son, never find fault with anyone, lest you see someone being honored and say, “This man has already received his comfort.”
Guard yourself against this thought, because it is very evil. For God hates the person who honors only himself while hating his brother.
But whoever says of himself, “I am somebody,” when he is nothing, deceives himself. Who will be able to help him
when he is proud, making his heart like the heart of God,
saying, “There is no one like me”? He will now hear his rebuke: “You will go down to Hades. They will throw you among the dead. They will spread maggots beneath you and cover you with worms.”
But the person who has acquired humility has judged himself, saying,
“My sins are greater than everyone else's.” He must not judge anyone or find fault with anyone. Who are you,
judging a servant who is not yours?
For the master of the one who has fallen has the power to make him stand.
Watch yourself, my son. Never find fault with anyone.
Taste all the virtues and hold on to them.
If you are a stranger, keep to yourself. Do not rush into people's company or involve yourself in their affairs.
You are poor. Do not lose heart in anything, lest you be rebuked, for “Poverty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly.” Have you not heard: “When you are hungry, you will become distressed,
and you will speak evil of the ruler and ancestral traditions”?
Watch out, too, lest they wage war against you over anything you lack for your bodily needs,
over food, and you lose heart. Instead, persevere. God is certainly already at work in secret.
Remember Habakkuk in Judea and Daniel in Chaldea.
For the distance between them amounts to forty stages of travel, and Daniel in particular was down at the bottom of the pit, as food for the wild beasts.
He prepared the meal for him.
Remember Elijah in the wilderness and the widow in Zarephath, upon whom the scourge of famine and the distress of hunger weighed heavily. Yet in her deprivation she did not lose heart.
Instead, she struggled and overcame, and she received the promises of God. Her household found prosperity in the time of famine.
Giving bread in a time of prosperity is no act of strength, nor is it poverty if you lose heart amid deprivation.
For it is written about the saints that they were in need, afflicted, and suffering.
For they boast in their afflictions.
If you persevere in the struggle described in the Scriptures, no slavery will come upon us, as it is written:
“Do not let anyone enslave you over food and drink, or regarding a festival, a new moon, or a Sabbath. These are a shadow of the things to come.”
Meditate at all times on the words of God, persevere in suffering, and give thanks in everything.
Flee from human honor, and love the person who corrects you in the fear of God.
Let everyone benefit you, so that you too may benefit everyone. Persevere in your good work and your good speech.
Do not take a step forward and a step backward, lest God hate you.
For the crown will belong to those who persevere. Obey God more and more, so that he may save you.
When you sit among the brothers, do not take pleasure in any foolish talk.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego rejected the pleasures of Nebuchadnezzar.
Therefore he could not draw them in with his musical instruments, nor could he deceive them with the food from his table.
Therefore they quenched his flame, which rose forty-nine cubits high. They did not change along with the one who changes.
Instead, they remained upright with the one who is upright, namely God. Therefore he made them rulers over their enemies.
Daniel too did not heed the evil reasoning of the Chaldeans. Therefore he became exceedingly distinguished.
And vigilance and wisdom were found in him. He shut the mouths of the wild lions.
Now then, my son, if you make God your hope, he will be your helper in your time of need.
For whoever approaches God must believe that he exists and that he will reward those who seek him.
These words were written for us so that we might believe in God and struggle, from small things to great, with fasting, prayers, and the rest of our worship,
down to the saliva that has dried up in your mouth during a fast.
God will not forget it. Rather, you will find all these things in your time of need. Only—
Humble yourself in everything.
Hold back your words, even if you understand everything, and remain at peace.
Do not consider yourself dishonored, but endure every trial with joy. For if you knew the honor that follows trials,
you would not pray, “Take them away from me.” For it is better for you to pray, weep, and groan until you are saved than to let your guard down and be taken captive.
O man, what are you doing in Babylon? You have grown old in a foreign land because you did not see fit to hold on to God in uprightness.
Therefore, my brother, do not let your guard down.
Perhaps you forget for a little while,
but your enemies neither sleep nor forget. Night and day they devise deceit against you.
Therefore, do not pursue greatness, lest you be humbled and your enemies rejoice over you.
Instead, pursue humility, for whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
If you cannot manage on your own, attach yourself to someone who lives by the gospel of Christ, and you will make progress with him.
Either obey or submit to someone who obeys. Either be strong and be called Elijah, or obey the strong and be called Elisha.
Because he obeyed Elijah, Elijah’s spirit came upon him in double measure.
If you want to live among people, imitate Abraham, Lot, Moses, and Samuel.
If you want to live in the wilderness, look: all the prophets are before you.
Imitate them as they wander in deserts, caves, and holes in the earth, suffering deprivation, affliction, and hardship.
He also said, “The shadow of the thirsty and the spirit of those who suffer oppression will bless you.”
Now the robber spoke a word on the cross, and the Lord forgave his sins and took him into paradise.
See how great your honor will be if you endure a trial, a spirit of sexual immorality, a spirit of pride, or any other passion.
Simply struggle against the devil’s passions that draw you after him,
and Jesus will grant you what he has promised.
Guard yourself against forgetfulness, for it is the mother of all failures.
My son, flee from desire, for it darkens the mind.
It does not allow the mind to know the mystery of God.
And it makes you a stranger to the language of the Spirit.
And it does not let you carry the cross of Christ.
And it does not let your heart stay alert to God's blessings.
Guard yourself against the appetite of the belly, which alienates you from the good things of paradise.
Guard yourself against impurity, which angers God and his angels.
My son, turn to God and love him. Flee from the enemy and hate him, so that God's gifts may be yours and you may inherit the blessing of Judah, the son of Jacob.
For he said, “Judah, your brothers will bless you. Your hands will be over the pride of your enemies, and your father's sons will serve you.”
Guard yourself against pride, for it is the beginning of every evil.
The beginning of pride is withdrawing from God; what follows it is hardness of heart.
If you guard yourself against these things, your resting place is the heavenly Jerusalem.
If the Lord loves you and honors you,
be on your guard. Do not become proud, but remain humble, so that you may remain in the honor God has given you.
Be watchful and sober, for blessed is the one who is found watching: he will be put in charge of his master's possessions.
And he will enter the kingdom rejoicing, and the bridegroom's friends will love him, because he was found watching over his vineyard.
My son, be patient in everything, for it is written, “Be diligent to present yourself to God as someone approved, a worker who has no cause for shame.”
Press forward toward God like someone who sows and someone who reaps, and you will gather God's good things into your storehouse.
Do not put on a show like the hypocrites. Instead, renounce the desires of your heart and work for God, while working for your own salvation.
If a passion troubles you through greed, envy, hatred, or any of the other passions, be sober and take on the heart of a lion.
Take on a strong heart, fight against them, and overthrow them like Sihon, Og, and all the kings of the Amorites.
Then the beloved, only-begotten Son, King Jesus, will fight on your behalf, and you will inherit the cities of your enemies.
But cast every kind of pride away from yourself and be courageous.
See how, when Joshua son of Nun became courageous, God delivered his enemies into his hands.
If you become fainthearted, you become a stranger to God's law.
Faintheartedness fills you with excuses, [?], unbelief, and negligence, until you perish.
Have the heart of a lion, and cry out yourself, “Who can separate us from the love of God?” And say, “Even if my outer self is wasting away, my inner self is being renewed day by day.”
If you are in the desert, struggle with prayers, fasts, and affliction.
If you are among people, be wise like snakes and innocent like doves.
If someone insults you, bear with him in silence and put your hope in God, for he will act for your good.
But you must not dishonor the image of God, for he is the one who said, “Whoever honors me, I will honor; whoever dishonors me, I will dishonor.”
And if people honor you, do not rejoice, for it is written, “Woe to you when everyone honors you.”
He also said, “Blessed are you when people harass you, persecute you, and reject your name as evil.”
Consider also our fathers Barnabas and Paul: when people honored them, they tore their clothes and grieved, hating human praise.
Peter, too, and John, when they were insulted in the council, went out rejoicing,
because they had been counted worthy to be insulted for the Lord’s holy name, placing their hope in honor in heaven.
But you, my son, flee from the comfort of this age so that you may enjoy yourself in the age to come.
Do not be careless, putting off one day after another, lest they overtake you before you realize it, and you reach the threshold of your ordeal, and these shape-shifters
surround you, seize you mercilessly, and take you to their dark places, which are full of terror and distress.
Do not grieve when people insult you. Instead, grieve and sigh when you sin.
This is the real disgrace, and you go about with the wound of your sins.
I most earnestly command you to hate empty glory.
Vainglory is the devil’s weapon. This is how Eve was ensnared.
He said to her, “Eat from the tree; your eyes will [?], and you will become like the gods.”
She listened, thinking it was true, and pursued the glory of divinity.
Even her humanity was taken away from her.
But you too, if you pursue empty glory, it will estrange you from the glory of God.
As for Eve, no one had written to her to warn her about this battle beforehand, before the devil tempted her.
For this reason, the Word of God came and took flesh from Mary the virgin, to set Eve’s race free.
But you have been taught about this battle by the saints who came before you, through the holy Scriptures.
Therefore, my brother, do not say, “I have not heard,” or, “No one warned me beforehand, yesterday and the day before, day after day.”
For it is written, “Their voice has gone out over the whole earth, and their words have reached the ends of the inhabited world.”
So now, if people honor you, keep your heart under control and give glory to God.
And if people insult you, give glory to God and thank him because you have been found worthy to share the lot of his Son and his saints.
If they called your Lord a deceiver, and the prophets people who insult him, and others madmen, then how much more will they insult us, who are dust and ashes?
Do not be sad if people insult you. This is the way to your life.
But if it is your negligence that drags you along, then weep and mourn, for those who are mocked on the [?]
were covered with shame because they neglected the law of God and followed the desires of their hearts.
Now then, my son, weep before God at all times, for it is written: “Blessed is the one you have chosen and taken to yourself.
You have placed thoughts in his heart for the valley of weeping, the place you established.”
Acquire innocence for yourself, and become like these innocent sheep: their wool is taken from them, and they do not speak.
Do not move from place to place, saying, “I will find God in this place or that one.”
God said, “I fill heaven; I fill the earth.”
And again, “If you cross through water, I am with you, and the rivers will not drown you.”
Understand, my son, that God is within you, so that you may remain in the law and commandments of God.
Look at the robber on the cross: he went to paradise.
Look, on the other hand, at Judas among the apostles: he betrayed his Lord.
Look at Rahab in her prostitution:
she was counted among the saints.
Look, on the other hand, at Eve in paradise: she was enslaved.
Look at Job on the dung heap: he was compared to his Lord.
Look, on the other hand, at Adam in paradise: he departed from the commandment.
Look at the angels of heaven: they were taken down to the abyss.
Look, on the other hand, at Elijah and Enoch: they were taken to the kingdom of heaven. So, in every place,
seek God and seek his face at all times.
Seek him as Abraham did: he obeyed God and offered up his son as a sacrifice to God.
He called him “my friend.”
Seek him as Joseph did, who struggled against lust until he ruled over his enemies.
Seek him as Moses did, who followed his Lord.
He made him a lawgiver and showed him his own form.
Daniel sought him, and he revealed great mysteries to him.
He rescued him from the mouths of the lions.
The three holy men sought him and found him in the fiery furnace.
Job ran to him, and he healed him of his affliction.
Susanna sought him, and he saved her from the hands of the lawless men.
Judith sought him and found him in the tent of Holofernes.
All these sought him, and he saved them. He saved others too.
And you, my son, how long will you remain careless?
What is the end of your carelessness?
As last year was, so is this year too.
As yesterday was, so is today too.
How long will you remain careless? You will make no progress.
Be alert and awaken your heart.
For you too must be brought before God's judgment seat and give an account of what you have done in secret and what you have done openly.
If you go to a place belonging to God where there is spiritual warfare, and the Spirit of God warns you,

saying, “Do not sleep in this place, because there is a trap in it,” and the devil, for his part, coaxes you, saying, “What happened to you the first time?” or, “Even if you see something, you will not be distressed,”
do not listen to his deceitful talk, lest the Spirit of God withdraw from you
and you become weak and powerless like Samson, and the Philistines bind you and take you to the grinding place, which is the gnashing of teeth,
and you become a laughingstock to them—that is, they rejoice over you—and you no longer know the way to your city because your eyes have been gouged out.
This is because you opened your heart to Delilah, that is, the devil, who took you by deceit because you abandoned the Spirit's counsel.
You have also seen what she did to that mighty, courageous, wise David: he quickly repented over Uriah's wife.
It is also written, “You have seen my severity; be afraid.”
Look, you have been told that he did not spare the holy ones.

Be alert, then, and watch your steps. Flee from this persistent one and separate yourself from him, lest he gouge out the eyes of your mind and make you blind, so that you no longer know the way to the city where you belong.
Again: Know the city of Christ and glorify him, because he died for you.
Why, when a brother speaks a word against you, do you become angry and act like a wild beast toward him?
Do you not remember that Christ died for you?
Yet when your enemy, the devil, whispers to you, you turn your ear toward him, and he pours filth down into it.
You open your heart and swallow the poison he has thrown to you.
You poor wretch! This is the time to become a wild beast, or to become like a fire until you have burned up all his malice.
Tear open your heart and cast out the stench of lawlessness, lest the poison pierce you and you die.
O man, you could not bear a little word that your brother spoke against you.
But when your enemy seeks to devour your soul, what have you done?
You have grown careless toward him. No, my beloved! Do not let it be proclaimed about you that instead of a golden ornament for the head, they will shave your head because of your deeds.
Instead, be vigilant and cheerfully bear with anyone who insults you. Be patient with your brother, and do not be afraid of bodily suffering.
My son, pay attention to the words of the wise Paul, as he says, “Chains and afflictions await me in Jerusalem.”
“But I do not consider my life valuable in any way, so that I may finish my course.”
And: “I am ready to die in Jerusalem for the name of my Lord Jesus Christ.”
For neither suffering nor temptation prevented the saints from going to the Lord.
So strengthen yourself and be strong. What have you to do with the devil’s cowardice?
Instead, pursue the courage of the saints.
My son, why are you fleeing from Adonai, the Lord of hosts?
Yet you are running after captivity among the Chaldeans.
Why do you set your heart on eating with demons?
My son, guard yourself against sexual immorality.
Do not corrupt the members of Christ.
Do not listen to the demons and make the members of Christ into the members of a prostitute.
Remember the anguish of the punishments.
Set God’s judgment before you and flee from every desire.
Strip yourself of the old self and its deeds, and put on the new self.
Remember the distress of the moment when you leave the body.
My son, run to God, for he is the one who created you, and he endured these sufferings for your sake.
For he said, “I gave my back to whips and my cheeks to blows. I did not turn my face away from shame and spitting.”
O man, what business have you on the road to Egypt, drinking water from the muddy Gihon?
What business have you with these troubled thoughts?
[?] until these sufferings overtake you.
Instead, sit down and weep for your sins.
For it is written, “If you make an offering for your sins, your souls will see long-lived offspring.”
Do you see, then, O man, that transgression is evil, and how much suffering and distress sin produces?
O man, hurry! Flee from sin and remember the hour of death.
For it is written, “The wise person humbles sin,” and, “The faces of those who practice self-discipline will shine like the sun.”
Remember Moses too: he chose to suffer with the people of God rather than enjoy sin for a time.
If you love the suffering of the saints, they will become your companions and intercede for you before God.
And he will grant you every good request, because you have taken up your cross and followed your Lord.
Do not pursue a seat of human honor, so that God may shelter you from the storm you do not know about and restore you to his capital city, the heavenly Jerusalem.
Test everything as well.
Hold firmly to what is good. Likewise, do not be blind to the image of God.
Guard your youth as well, so that you may safeguard your old age, lest you be put to shame and feel remorse in the Valley of Jehoshaphat.
All God's creation will look at you and mock you, saying,
“We always thought you were a sheep, but here we have found you to be a wolf. Go now to the pit of Hades! Throw yourself now into the heart of the earth!”
Oh, the great shame of this deception! You walk about in the world, and people honor you as a chosen one. But when you come to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, the place of judgment, they find you naked.
And everyone sees your sins and your disgrace, exposed before God and human beings.
Woe to you at that hour! Where will you turn your face?
Or what will you open your mouth to say? Your sins are stamped on your soul, which is black as sackcloth.

What will you do at that hour? You will weep, but they will not accept your tears. You will plead, but they will not accept your pleas, because those into whose hands you have been delivered are merciless.
Oh, woe at the moment when you hear that terrifying, piercing voice: “Let sinners return to Hades!”
And again: “Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels.”
And again: “I have hated those who commit transgressions, so that I may destroy from the Lord’s city all who practice lawlessness.”
Now then, my son, make use of this world with detachment, living without guile.
Follow the Lord in everything, so that you may have confidence in the valley of Jehoshaphat.
Let people see you in the world as one of those who are rejected, but on the day of judgment let them find you clothed in glory.
Do not place your confidence in anyone for the well-being of your soul. Instead, cast your cares on the Lord, and he will sustain you.
Look at Elijah, who trusted in him beside the brook Cherith: he sustained him through a raven.
Guard yourself very carefully against sexual immorality, for it has seduced many and brought them down.
Do not make friends with a boy.
Do not seek intimacy with a woman.
Flee bodily comfort, for intimacy flares up like a fire.
Do not seek intimacy with anyone in the flesh, because when stone strikes steel, fire flares up and burns a great deal of fuel.
Run to the Lord at all times and sit beneath his shade, for whoever dwells in the protection of the Most High will remain beneath the shade of the God of heaven and will never be shaken.
Remember the Lord, and let the heavenly Jerusalem rise in your heart. You will dwell in heaven’s blessing, and the glory of God will carry you.
Guard your body and your heart with the utmost care.
Pursue peace and purity, bound together, so that you may see God.
Do not bear a grudge against anyone, for whoever bears a grudge against his brother is an enemy of God.
And whoever is at peace with his brother is at peace with God.

Now, then, you understand that nothing is greater than peace, so that each person should love his brother. Even if you are pure from every sin, if you are an enemy of your brother, you are a stranger to God.
For it is written: “Seek peace and purity, for they are bound together.”
And again it is written: “Even if I have all faith, enough to move mountains, but have no love within me, I will gain nothing.”
Love builds up.
What will cleanse defilement? If there is hatred or hostility in your heart, where is your purity?
The Lord said through Jeremiah: “He speaks to his neighbor with peaceful words.”
But hostility is in his heart as he speaks deceitfully with his neighbor; hostility is in his heart, or he is thinking about hostility.
“Will I not be angry over these things?” says the Lord.
“Or will I not take vengeance on a nation like this?”
Thus he says that whoever is an enemy to his brother is that nation, because the nations walk in darkness and have not known the light.
So it is with someone who hates his brother: he walks in darkness and does not know God.
For the hatred of hostility has closed his eyes, and he cannot see the image of God.
But the Lord commands you, “Love your enemies. Bless those who curse you. Do good to those who persecute us.”
Then how great is the danger we are in when we hate one another, our fellow members joined with us, the children of God,
the branches of the true vine, the sheep of the spiritual fold, whom the true shepherd, the only Son of God, has gathered together,
having offered himself up as a sacrifice for us. This person of such great worth, for whom the living Word endured these sufferings—you, for your part, hate him!
O man, why are you jealous over empty glory,
or love of money, or greatness? These are the things through which the enemy has bound you, for he has made you a stranger to God.
What defense will you present to Christ? He will say to you, “Insofar as you hate your brother, it is me you hate.”
But you will go to eternal punishment because you are an enemy to your brother.
Your brother, however, will enter eternal life because he humbles himself before you for Jesus’ sake.
So let us seek a remedy for the wound before we die.
My beloved, let us run to the gospel, the true law of God, Christ, and we will hear him saying, “Do not condemn, so that you will not be condemned.”
“Forgive, and you will be forgiven.”
If you will not forgive, you too will not be forgiven.
If you are going to hold a grudge against your brother, prepare yourself for punishments for your offenses, for your transgression, for the acts of sexual immorality you commit,
the thefts, your lies, your frivolous words, your evil thoughts, your greed, and your evil deeds, for which you will give an account before the judgment seat of Christ,
while all God’s creation watches you, and all the angels and the entire army stand there,
with their swords drawn, compelling you to make your defense and confess your sins,
while all your clothing is filthy and your mouth is shut, and you are dumb, with nothing to say. For how many things will you have to give an account?
Oh, the misery of so much sexual immorality, which is a [?] to your soul, the desires of the eyes,
the evil thoughts that trouble the spirit and bring grief to the soul, the appetite of the mouth, the tongue that utters great boasts and defiles the whole body!
Fits of rage, evil [?], slander, jealousy, hatred, deceit, mockery of the image of God;
the ugliness of desires like these, which have stripped away the good things of paradise; the thieving passions that [?] over them; evil thoughts against the image of God;
anger, contentiousness, shamelessness, impudence, the malicious thoughts of your heart, mercilessness, arrogance.
You will be questioned about all these things because you held a grudge against your brother and did not resolve it, as you were obliged to do, in the love of God.
Have you yourself not heard that love covers a multitude of sins?
And that this is what your Father in heaven will do to you: if you do not forgive one another from your heart, your Father in heaven will not forgive your sins.
Look, my beloved, you know that we have clothed ourselves with Christ, who is good and loves humanity.
Let us not deprive ourselves of him because of our evil deeds, since we have promised God purity and have pledged ourselves to the monastic life.
Let us practice its works, which are these: fasting, unceasing prayer, purity of body, and purity of heart.
If we have promised God purity, let us not be caught in acts of sexual immorality in countless forms.
For he said, “They committed sexual immorality in many forms.”
Brothers, let us not be found engaged in deeds of this kind and be discovered beneath everyone else.
We have also pledged ourselves to become disciples of Christ.
Let us discipline ourselves through hardship, for hardship reduces defilement.
Now the contest lies before us. Let us not give up, so that we do not become slaves to sin.
We have been appointed to give light to the world. Let no one stumble because of you. Let us maintain silence.
For many have been saved through this. Be sober-minded, brothers!
Let us not call one another to account, so that we are not called to account at the hour of punishment, whether you are virgins, renunciants, or hermits.
Nevertheless, he will say to us, “Give back what is mine, with its interest.” He will find fault with us and say to us, “Where is the wedding garment?
Where is the light of the lamps?
If you are my son, where is your fear of me?
If you hated me in this world, then get away from me, for I do not know you.
If you hated your brother, then you are a stranger to my kingdom.
If you held a grudge against your brother and did not forgive him, then they will bind
your hands behind you, along with your feet, and throw you into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
If you struck your brother, you will be handed over to merciless angels, and they will scourge you with fiery whips forever.
You did not honor my image. You showed contempt, acted arrogantly, and shamed me.
For this reason, I will not honor you in your time of distress.
[?] you did not make peace with your brother in this world.
I too will have nothing to do with you on the day of the great judgment.
You despised the poor person. It is me you are insulting.
You struck the needy person. You too are a companion of the one who struck me during my humiliation on the cross.
Did I demand anything from you during my stay in the world?
Did I not freely give you my body and my blood as life-giving food?
Did I not taste death for you so that I could redeem you?
Did I not reveal to you the mystery of heaven, so that I could make you my brother and companion?
Did I not give you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy?
Did I not give you many life-giving remedies through which you would be saved?
My mighty deeds, my signs, and my wonders, which I performed in the world, are weapons of warfare.
I gave them to you so that you could arm yourself with them and strike down Goliath, who is the devil.
Now what do you lack, that you should become a stranger to me?
It is your own negligence alone that has thrown you into the pit of Hades.
Now then, my son, these things and greater things than these are what we will hear if we are negligent and do not obey the command to forgive one another.
Let us be vigilant.
And let us recognize the virtues of God, which will help us on the day of death, these guides in the midst
of the fierce and terrifying battle, these things that raise the soul from the dead.
First, we were given faith and knowledge so that we could cast out the unbelief within us.
Afterward, we were given wisdom and understanding so that we could recognize the devil's schemes, flee from him, and hate him.
Fasting, prayer, and self-control were preached to us. These will give the body a bridle and a curb through suffering.
We were given purity and vigilance, because of which God will dwell in us.
We were given patience and gentleness. If we guard all these things, we will inherit the glory of God.
We were given love and peace, which are powerful in battle, for no enemy can slip into the place where these are.
We were instructed about joy, so that through it we might fight against sorrow.
We were also taught generosity and kindness.
We were given holy prayer and perseverance, which fill the soul with light.
We were given humility and prudence, which crush wickedness.
We were instructed in writing not to judge, so that we might overcome deceit, this evil disposition within human beings.
For if we do not judge, we will not be judged on the day of judgment.
For endurance of suffering and acceptance of injustices were given to us so that vindictiveness would not sprout up again.
For our fathers lived out their lives in hunger, thirst, and many hardships until they attained purity.
Above all, they fled from wine-drinking, which is full of every kind of harm.
These disturbances, these tumults, and these disorders are in our bodily members because of excessive wine.
It is a fury full of sins, the [?] and the [?] of the fruits.
For the pleasure of insatiability makes the mind foolish, makes the conscience shameless, and tears away the tongue’s bridle.
The greatest joy of all is not to grieve the Holy Spirit or to become drunk on pleasure.
For he said, “The priest and the prophet have become drunk because of wine.”
Wine is unrestrained, and strong drink is disgraceful. Whoever gives himself over to these will not remain pure from sin.
Wine is good if you drink it in moderation. If you set your eyes on bowls and cups, you will walk about naked like a pestle.
Therefore, let everyone who has prepared to become a disciple of Jesus abstain from wine and strong drink.
For our fathers knew the great harm that would come from wine, and they abstained from it. They would drink only a little because of illness.
For if a little was permitted to the great worker Timothy, whose body suffered from many illnesses,
then the one who seethes with wickedness in the ranks of childhood, upon whom the defilements of the passions abound—
what am I to say to them? I am afraid to say, “Do not let him drink at all,” lest someone who hates his own salvation grumble against me.
For these words are difficult for many people of this time.
Nevertheless, my beloved, it is good to be watchful, and hardship is beneficial. For whoever subjects himself to hardship—
He will bring his ship safely into the good and holy harbor of salvation, and he will be satisfied with the good things of heaven.
But greater than all these, we have been given humility, which guards all the virtues. Humility is this great and holy power with which God clothed himself when he came into the world.
The bulwark of the virtues, the treasury of good deeds, the saving weapon, the healer of every sorrow.
When they had made these [?] and these gold objects of the tabernacle and all these ornaments, they covered them with a covering of haircloth.
He is insignificant in people's eyes, but chosen and honored in God's eyes.
If we acquire it for ourselves, we will trample on all the power of the enemy.
For he said, “I will look upon no one except the humble and the gentle.”
Let us not lose heart in this time of [?], because boasting and flattery have increased.
Greed has increased. Sexual immorality has become king through the gratification of the flesh. Arrogance has taken command.
The young have stopped obeying their elders, and the elders have given up caring for the young. Each person has followed the desires of his own heart.
Now is the time for us to cry out with the prophet, “Woe to me, my soul, for the God-fearing person has perished from the earth.”
And there was no one among people who was upright according to Christ—that is, there is none at all. And, “Each person has oppressed his neighbor.”
Strive, my beloved, for the time has drawn near and the days have grown few. There is no father teaching his children, and no child obeying his father.
The good virgins have departed. The holy fathers everywhere have fallen asleep. The mothers have departed like these widows. We have become like orphans.
They have trampled on the humble and struck the heads of the poor.
Therefore, it is only a little while before God's wrath comes and we mourn with no one to comfort us.
All these things have happened to us because we have not subjected ourselves to hardship.
Let us strive, my beloved, so that we may receive the crown that has been prepared.
The throne is set out. The door of the kingdom is open. “To the one who conquers, I will give some of the hidden manna.”
If we strive and overcome the passions, we will reign forever. But if they overcome us, we will mourn and weep bitterly.
Let us fight against ourselves as long as repentance remains available to us.
Let us bear hardship so that we may be renewed in purity. Let us love humanity,
so that we may become friends of Jesus, who loves humanity.
If we have vowed to God to live the monastic life in love,
it is not merely bodily virginity, but a virginity that abstains from every sin.
For some virgins were turned away in the Gospel because of their negligence. Those who keep watch steadfastly enter the bridal chamber.
May everyone, then, enter that place forever.
The love of money, over which they fight against us.
If you want to acquire possessions for yourself—these things that are moths—and experience the fire through excessive greed,
whether through trading, robbery, usury, or so much manual work that you have no time to serve God—in any case,
if you have desired to accumulate gold or money for yourself, remember what he said in the Gospel:
“Fool! Tonight they will take your soul from you. And whose will the things you have prepared be?”
Likewise, also: “He accumulates things without knowing for whom he is accumulating them.”
Struggle, my dear friend, and resist this passion.
Say, “I will do as Abraham did. I will reach up to God Most High, who made heaven and earth,
and I will take nothing of all that belongs to you, from a thread to a sandal strap.”
A humble foreigner is a great blessing, and the Lord loves a foreigner, giving him bread and clothing.
As for the faintheartedness over which they also fight against us, saying, “Store things up for some need,”
remember that it is written: “Your storehouses will be cursed, and so will what is in them.”
And concerning gold and money, James said, “Their corrosion will testify against you, and the corrosion will consume your flesh like fire.”
And: “A righteous man who has no idol is better, as he sees their turmoil.”
Cleanse yourself also of anything accursed before the Lord calls you. For you have placed your hope in God, since it is written, “Let your hearts be pure and completely devoted to God.”
I greet you, my dear friend, in the Lord.
For you have made God your helper. You have become dear to him; you have set your heart on walking in God's commandments.
May God himself bless you, and may your spring become a river for you, and may the river also become a sea for them.
For you are a chariot, and you are a horseman of self-control. God's lamp is burning above you, and you shine with the hidden light of your spirit,
managing your words with judgment.
May God grant you the discernment of the saints, and may no idol be found in your city.
May you set your foot on the neck of the rulers of darkness,
and may you see the commander of the Lord's army standing at your right hand.
And drown Pharaoh and his army.
And bring your people across the salt sea, which is this life. Amen.
After these things, I again command you not to lose heart. For this is what delights the demons: that a person should lose heart, so that they can lead him into a trap before he realizes it.
So do not neglect to learn the fear of the Lord.
And grow like young plants.
And you will please God like a young calf putting forth horns and hooves.
Also be a strong person in deed and word.
Do not put on a show like the hypocrites, lest your portion be assigned with theirs.
Do not waste a single day of your life. Consider what you will give God each and every day.
Sit by yourself like a wise ruler and judge your thoughts, whether you live in solitude or among others.
In any case, judge yourself every day.
For it is better to be among a thousand people in complete humility than to be alone in a hyena’s den, living in pride.
It was testified of Lot, while he was among the people of Sodom, that he was a good, faithful man.
But we have also heard about Cain that there was no one on earth with him except three other people, yet he became wicked.
Now, then, the struggle is set before you. Examine what comes upon you each day, to see whether you are counted among us or among those who fight against us.
The demons do not come to you only from the right; the left is obvious to everyone.
For truly, they also fought against me from the right. They brought me the devil bound like a wild donkey. But the Lord helped me.
I did not fear them, nor did I lose heart because of them.
And many times they provoked us with the devil’s deeds from the right. He rushed at me, and he even dared to tempt the Lord. But the Lord crushed him and his schemes.
Now, then, my son, clothe yourself in humility, and make Christ your counselor, together with his good Father.
And befriend a man of God who has God’s law in his heart.
And make yourself like a poor man carrying his cross, with weeping as his companion.
And make yourself poor too, with a cloth on your head. Let your dwelling become a tomb for you until God raises you and gives you the crown of victory.
If you ever become angry with a brother who troubles you with something he says,
or your heart becomes embittered against a brother, and you say, “He does not deserve these things,”
Or the enemy works on you against someone, saying, “He does not deserve these honors,” and you accept what he says.
Or a thought comes from the devil, and the battle in your mind grows intense,
and you quarrel with your brother, knowing that there is no balm in Gilead and no physician around you.
Now turn toward quietness and awareness of God,
and weep alone with Christ. The Spirit of Jesus will speak with you in your mind
and rebuke you concerning the commandment, saying, “What need is there for you to fight alone, resembling a wild beast, as though this poison were inside you?
Remember that you too have fallen many times.
Have you not heard Christ saying, ‘Forgive your brother seventy-seven times’?
Do you not often weep yourself, pleading, ‘Forgive me for my many sins’?
Yet now you hold your brother’s little fault against him.”
Immediately the Spirit of God brings judgment before you, along with the fear of punishments.
And you remember the saints, that they were considered worthy of being insulted.
And you remember Christ, that he was insulted.
They spat on him and mocked him for your sake.
Immediately he fills your heart with compassion and fear, and you fall on your face, weeping and saying, “Forgive me, my Lord, for I have caused suffering to your image.”
Immediately you rise in the comfort of repentance
and run to your brother,
with your heart set free,
your face radiant and your mouth full of joy,
with peace surrounding you, smiling and greeting your brother affectionately: “Forgive me, my brother, for I have caused you suffering.”
Then the weeping increases, and great joy comes from the weeping.
Peace rejoices among you, and the Spirit of God himself rejoices and cries out, saying,
“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.”
When the enemy hears the sound of this cry, he is put to shame.
And God is glorified, and a great blessing comes to you.
Now then, my brother, let us struggle against ourselves, knowing that sluggishness has spread everywhere.
The churches are full of quarrelsome and angry people.
The communities of monks have become ambitious. Pride reigns.
No one speaks a word of encouragement to his neighbor. Instead, everyone harasses his neighbor.
We have fallen into the midst of these troubles.
There is neither a prophet nor anyone with spiritual understanding.
No one rebukes anyone, because hardheartedness has increased.
But anyone who understands will keep silent, because this is an evil time.
Everyone has made himself king. They show contempt where they should not.
Now then, my brother, make peace with your brother, and pray for me
too, because I cannot do any work, but I am troubled by my desires.
But you, be sober-minded in everything.
Endure hardship. Do the work of an evangelist. Persevere through temptation. Complete the struggle of the monastic life,
remaining humble and cheerful, trembling at the words you have heard, and guarding your virginity,
and keeping yourself from excess and these empty, alien voices.
Do not stray outside the writings of the saints, but remain firm in faith in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Through him, glory be to him and to his good Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. [?] Amen.
Bless us.
Through the diligence and care of our God-loving brother Michael, son of the blessed Stephen, the farmer of Moui, a man from the plain north of the city of Esna,
he had this book produced through his own hard work.
He donated it to the monastery of Saint Mercurius on the mountain of the city of Edfu, for the salvation of his soul, so that it might be read in the name
of Saint John and the holy Apa Pachomius, so that Saint Mercurius, the military commander and mighty martyr, and Saint
John the Baptist and forerunner of Christ, and Saint Apa Pachomius the archimandrite, might appeal to Christ on his behalf,
and he might bless him in this world, save him from all the snares of the devil and of evil people, and help him in every good undertaking.
Then, after he departs this life, may he be worthy of the forgiveness of his sins and receive an inheritance with all the saints. So be it. Amen.
Remember me too, Theopistus, the [?] deacon, son of Severus, the archpriest of Saint Mercurius in the city of Esna.
I wrote this book with my own hand. Pray for me, that God may forgive me the multitude of my sins, for they are very many. So be it.
Written in the month of [?], on the 16th, in the 15th indiction, in the year 701 of the holy martyrs, [?]. + Abba Nicodemus, from [?] the city of Apollonius [?].
